record.paper_title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems
record.original_question: Given a connected graph G, a spanning tree T is a tree 3-spanner when every pair of vertices x and y has tree distance d_T(x, y) at most 3 times graph distance d_G(x, y). A graph is chordal when it has no chordless cycle of length at least four, and a graph is strongly chordal when it is chordal and has no induced k-sun for any k >= 3. Is there an efficient algorithm to decide whether a chordal graph, and in particular whether a strongly chordal graph, admits a tree 3-spanner?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. For vertices x, y ∈ V, let d_G(x, y) denote the length (number of edges) of a shortest path between x and y in G. A spanning tree T of G is called a tree 3-spanner of G if, for every pair of vertices x, y ∈ V, the distance d_T(x, y) in T satisfies d_T(x, y) ≤ 3 · d_G(x, y).

A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle of length at least 4. For an integer k ≥ 3, a k-sun is the graph on 2k vertices consisting of a cycle u_1, w_1, u_2, w_2, …, u_k, w_k, u_1 together with all edges of a clique on {u_1, …, u_k}, where each w_i has degree exactly 2. A graph is strongly chordal if it is chordal and contains no induced k-sun for any k ≥ 3.

The Tree 3-Spanner problem on a graph class C asks: given G ∈ C, decide whether G admits a tree 3-spanner.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that decides Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is chordal? In particular, does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm deciding Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is strongly chordal?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate the complexity of deciding Tree 3-Spanner on chordal graphs, and even on the subclass of strongly chordal (undirected path) graphs, is still listed as an open problem. Positive polynomial-time results are known for several subclasses (very strongly chordal graphs, 1-split graphs, interval graphs, split graphs, chordal graphs of diameter ≤ 2, chordal bipartite graphs, etc.), and Tree t-Spanner is known to be NP-complete on chordal graphs for t ≥ 4, but no resolution of the t = 3 case on chordal/strongly chordal graphs was found.

status_evidence.title: Tree spanners on chordal graphs: complexity and algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity status of Tree 3-Spanner still remains open for chordal graphs, even on the subclass of undirected path graphs that are strongly chordal.
status_evidence.claim: Tree 3-Spanner on chordal and strongly chordal graphs is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: A linear time algorithm for constructing tree 3-spanner in simple chordal bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Linear time algorithm for tree 3-spanner on a subclass; status on chordal remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial/linear-time results exist for restricted subclasses, but not for the general chordal case.
